headline: Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since August and is heading for a sixth straight weekly loss, as rate-hike fears, money leaving bitcoin funds and over $1 billion of forced liquidations hit crypto.

market.asOf: Read about 03:54 UTC Sat 14 Nov (10:54 Bangkok) from CoinGecko. Prices have moved since; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 20, Extreme Fear, on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (28 the day before); CoinMarketCap's own index read 19.

stories.title: Bitcoin hits its lowest since August and heads for a sixth weekly loss
stories.summary: Bitcoin touched about $66,900 this week, its lowest level since 19 August, and is on course for a sixth losing week in a row. A stronger US dollar and expectations of a Fed rate hike in December are pulling money away from risky assets like crypto.
points: Bitcoin's low was $66,915 on Binance, the lowest since 19 August, per BigGo Finance.
Bitcoin is on track for a sixth straight weekly decline; the record is nine weeks, set in 2022, per CoinDesk.
CoinDesk puts bitcoin down about 11% in November and 21% so far this year.
The US Dollar Index rose above 103, its highest since April 2025, per Bitcoin Magazine.
Ether fell below $2,000 for the first time since August, per CryptoTicker.

stories.title: Over $1.4 billion of leveraged bets wiped out as prices fell
stories.summary: Traders who borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced to close their positions as bitcoin dropped. When that happens, exchanges sell automatically, which can push prices down faster. Totals differ by source and by the time they were counted.
points: CoinDesk counted $1.64B liquidated in 24 hours, about 88.7% of it bets on rising prices, with $916M on bitcoin.
An earlier CoinGlass count reported by The Block was $1.47B across 175,299 traders.
The largest single liquidation was a bitcoin bet worth more than $31M on Hyperliquid, per CryptoTicker.
Funding rates turned moderately negative, meaning traders betting on falling prices were paying those betting on rises, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Money keeps leaving bitcoin funds as rate-hike odds climb
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the way many Americans hold bitcoin in a brokerage account, have had a run of daily outflows. Markets now see a December Fed rate hike as very likely, and the money stablecoins hold has been shrinking. Separately, MSCI will drop bitcoin-buying company Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes after 30 November.
points: Figures for 12 November differ: $284M of net outflows, the sixth day in a row, per SoSoValue data reported by PANews; a preliminary $47.7M per Farside data cited by Bitcoin Magazine.
Wholesale prices (PPI) rose 0.3% in October against 0.4% expected, but 6.5% from a year earlier, per TokenPost.
Odds of a quarter-point December hike are high but differ by source: 91% after the PPI release in money markets, per TokenPost; 88% on CME FedWatch, per Bitcoin Magazine.
Stablecoin supply fell $14.2B over 30 days, the largest drop since June 2022, per Glassnode data reported by KuCoin.
MSCI removes Strategy after the close on 30 November, per The Block.

briefs.title: Anthropic IPO next week
briefs.summary: Anthropic's IPO could raise up to $64.4B plus a $26B private placement, per CoinDesk, which says it may be drawing money away from bitcoin.

briefs.title: US moves to seize $1.2B from North Korea's Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department has court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack, per The Block.

briefs.title: SEC and CFTC nominees sent to the Senate
briefs.summary: Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC and Matthew Rowland and Nathan Anonick to the CFTC; Senate confirmation is pending, per BlockBeats via KuCoin.

briefs.title: Visa adds stablecoin settlement
briefs.summary: Eligible businesses can settle on VisaNet using USDPT, a stablecoin issued by Anchorage Digital Bank, per Decrypt via BigGo. This is for business settlement, not everyday card payments.

briefs.title: Prediction-market fights spread
briefs.summary: Louisiana sued Kalshi, Polymarket and others, and Kalshi is reportedly discussing funding at a $65B valuation, per KuCoin. Separately, the US government and CFTC are suing Arkansas over its crackdown, per InvestmentNews.

briefs.title: Bitmine reports a $6.23B annual loss
briefs.summary: The ether treasury company's loss for the year to 31 August came mainly from ether's fall, per Yahoo Finance's weekly wrap.

briefs.title: Strategy keeps buying
briefs.summary: Strategy holds 850,364 BTC after buying 1,036 BTC for $81.9M in the week to 6 November, per Yahoo Finance's weekly wrap.

briefs.title: Big monthly options expiry on 27 November
briefs.summary: About $5.6B of bitcoin options expire on Deribit on 27 November, per CryptoTicker.
